'''Potato salad''' is able to trace its origins to Germany before the turn of the 17th century, where it first became popular to use vinegar and spices on the potato as a side to a meal. The salad has a bite to it and is served warm as often as not.

== Ingredients ==
* 2 [[Cookbook:Pound|pounds]] (3–4 [[Cookbook:Each|ea]].) medium [[Cookbook:Potato|russet potatoes]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] plus ½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Vinegar|distilled white vinegar]]
* 1 medium [[Cookbook:Celery|rib of celery]]
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] celery seed
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Mayonnaise|mayonnaise]]
* ¾ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Mustard|powdered mustard]]
* 2 tablespoons minced [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]]
* 2 tablespoons minced fresh [[Cookbook:Parsley|parsley leaves]]
* ¼ teaspoon ground [[Cookbook:Black Pepper|black pepper]]
* 3 tablespoons sweet pickle relish

== Procedure ==
# Peel and cut potatoes into ¾ [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] cubes.
# Cover potatoes with an [[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] of water in a large saucepan and bring to a [[Cookbook:Boil|boil]].
# Add 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] salt to boiling water and reduce heat to medium.
# [[Cookbook:Simmer|Simmer]] about 8 minutes, stirring gently once or twice, until potatoes are tender. Taste a piece—don't overcook.
# Drain potatoes and place in a large bowl.
# [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] potatoes gently with vinegar using a rubber [[Cookbook:Spatula|spatula]].
# Cool potatoes. They must be no more than barely warm to mix.
# [[Cookbook:Chop|Chop]] celery fine.
# Stir together celery, celery seeds, mayonnaise, dry mustard, onion, parsley, pepper, and ½ teaspoon salt.
# Gently [[Cookbook:Folding|fold]] together dressing mix and potatoes.
# Cover and refrigerate at least an hour, until thoroughly chilled.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* You may have to substitute celery salt for the celery seeds, but then leave out the salt in the dressing.
* Do not mix too much once the potatoes are in, or they will break down.
* A couple of hard-boiled eggs, diced about ¼ inch may be added when the final mix is made.
